attacks.claim: Social-security disputes go to the social section (cpca 500 ¶7) but do not pass through a conciliation office: Law 08-08 makes a prior internal recourse mandatory (art. 4) and then gives only 30 days from delivery of the notification of the national prior-recourse commission's decision, or 60 days from its receipt of the petition when no reply comes, to bring the case before the court (art. 15). The record knows only the six-month period from a non-conciliation record; for such a claim nonconciliation_record is 'no', so d5 says nothing and the claim falls under d1's fifteen years.

source.what: Law 08-08 of 23 February 2008 on social-security disputes, Official Journal 2008 no. 11 (2 March 2008), p. 8 (art. 2 to 5) and p. 9 (art. 13 to 15). Also cpca 500 ¶7, Official Journal 2008 no. 21, p. 41 (https://www.joradp.dz/FTP/JO-ARABE/2008/A2008021.pdf). Not checked: whether Law 08-08 was amended later; the amendment ledger does not cover it.

attacks.quoteArabic: المادة 4 : ترفع الخلافات المتعلقة بالمنازعات العامة إجباريا أمام لجان الطعن المسبق، قبل أي طعن أمام الجهات القضائية. ... المادة 15 : تكون القرارات الصادرة عن اللجنة الوطنية المؤهلة للطعن المسبق قابلة للطعن فيها أمام المحكمة المختصة طبقا لأحكام قانون الإجراءات المدنية، في أجل ثلاثين (30) يوما ابتداء من تاريخ تسليم تبليغ القرار المعترض عليه، أو في أجل ستين (60) يوما ابتداء من تاريخ استلام العريضة من طرف اللجنة الوطنية المؤهلة للطعن المسبق إذا لم يتلق المعني أي رد على عريضته.
attacks.consequence: A social-security claim (insured person or employer against a social-security body) has its own 30-day or 60-day filing period and a mandatory prior recourse; the record gives it no deadline and, through d1, a fifteen-year horizon. A lawyer would be told nothing while a 30-day period runs out. The record must at least recognise this case and not treat 'no non-conciliation record' as 'no filing deadline' for the social section.

attacks.claim: The Civil Code itself sets a three-year limitation for every action arising from an insurance contract, running from the event that gave rise to it (art. 624), with its own delayed starting points (concealment or false declaration: from the insurer's knowledge; occurrence of the insured event: from the knowledge of those concerned). The record does not cite it; an insured person's claim against his insurer is answered by d1 (fifteen years from the due date), so a claim three to fifteen years old gets no warning at all.

source.what: Ordinance 75-58 of 26 September 1975 (Civil Code), art. 624, Official Journal 1975 no. 78 (30 September 1975), Arabic p. 1030; French edition p. 849 (https://www.joradp.dz/FTP/JO-FRANCAIS/1975/F1975078.pdf: « Les actions nées du contrat d'assurance se prescrivent par trois années à partir de la date de l'événement qui leur a donné naissance »). Art. 624 is not in the amendment ledger. Lead, not read: Ordinance 95-07 on insurance (art. 27) is said to set the same three years.

attacks.quoteArabic: المادة 624 : تسقط بالتقادم الدعاوى الناشئة عن عقد التأمين بانقضاء ثلاث سنوات من وقت حدوث الواقعة التي تولدت عنها هذه الدعاوى. غير انه لا تسرى تلك المدة : - فى حالة اخفاء بيانات متعلقة بالخطر المؤمن منه أو تقديم بيانات غير صحيحة أو غير دقيقة عن هذا الخطر الا من اليوم الذى علم فيه المؤمن بذلك. - فى حالة وقوع الحادث المؤمن منه الا من اليوم الذى علم فيه ذوو الشأن بوقوعه.
attacks.consequence: Insurance-contract claims need their own deadline (three years from the generating event, with the two knowledge-based starts) or at least a question that takes them out of d1; as written, d1's fifteen years is wrong for them and the record is silent until fifteen years have passed.

attacks.claim: CPCA 504 forfeits the right to sue once six months from delivery of the record have run; the only way back is an order lifting the forfeiture (cpca 322), and the only extension is to the next working day when the last day is not one (cpca 405 ¶4). The record applies its 15-day warning band after expiry too, so a claim filed several working days late is shown only as a warning: ex19 (record delivered 2025-10-20, petition 2026-04-25) expects 'warn', although the last day (20/21 April 2026, Monday/Tuesday) is an ordinary working day and no reading of o4 or o7 saves it.

source.what: Law 08-09 of 25 February 2008 (CPCA), art. 504, Official Journal 2008 no. 21 (23 April 2008), p. 41. Art. 504 is not touched by Law 22-13 (amendment ledger).

attacks.quoteArabic: المادة 504 : يجب رفع الدعوى أمام القسم الاجتماعي في أجل لا يتجاوز ستة (6) أشهر من تاريخ تسليم محضر عدم الصلح، وذلك تحت طائلة سقوط الحق في رفع الدعوى.
attacks.consequence: After the last possible day under every recorded reading (day of delivery and day of expiry both excluded, then extended past any non-working day), d5 should block the clean export, not warn; the band can only cover the days the open points o4 and o7 make uncertain, not a fixed 15 days after expiry. ex19 expects the wrong effect.

attacks.claim: The Commercial Code is said to set short limitation periods for bills of exchange and cheques: three years from maturity for actions against the acceptor of a bill, one year and six months for recourse between holders and endorsers (art. 461), and six months from the end of the presentment period for the holder's recourse on a cheque (art. 527 or near). A claim for payment of an unpaid bill or cheque is answered by d1 with fifteen years.

source.what: My own memory of Ordinance 75-59 of 26 September 1975 (Commercial Code), arts. 461 and 527 (article numbers and wording not verified; not read on joradp.dz, Official Journal 1975 no. 101 not fetched). A lead only.

attacks.quoteArabic: (from memory, unverified) تتقادم كل الدعاوى الناتجة عن السفتجة ضد القابل بمضي ثلاث سنوات اعتبارا من تاريخ الاستحقاق
attacks.consequence: o9's protective reading (apply 308 and warn that a shorter period may apply) is only shown when d1 itself fires, i.e. after fifteen years; for bills and cheques the warning comes years too late. Check arts. 461 and 527 of the Commercial Code on the Official Journal and add them or a question that excludes these claims from d1.

attacks.claim: Code of Criminal Procedure art. 10 is said to provide that the civil action follows the Civil Code's limitation but may no longer be brought before the criminal court once the public action is time-barred. A victim of a harmful act that is also an offence (assault, road accident) therefore has a much shorter window for the civil-party route than d2's fifteen years.

source.what: My own memory of Ordinance 66-155 (Code of Criminal Procedure), art. 10 as amended (amending law not identified, not read on joradp.dz). A lead only.

attacks.quoteArabic: (from memory, unverified) تتقادم الدعوى المدنية وفق أحكام القانون المدني، غير أنه لا يجوز رفع هذه الدعوى أمام الجهة القضائية الجزائية بعد انقضاء أجل تقادم الدعوى العمومية.
attacks.consequence: This app files before the civil courts, so d2 stands for the petition itself; but d2's message should not let the lawyer believe fifteen years also holds for a civil-party claim before the criminal court. Verify art. 10 on the Official Journal.

attacks.claim: The French edition of art. 310 names more creditors than the Arabic one the record follows: dental surgeons, midwives and architects (« chirurgiens-dentistes, sages-femmes ... architectes »). The question for claim_is_professional_fees reads out a closed Arabic list; a lawyer for a midwife or an architect will likely answer 'no', and d6's two years is then replaced by d1's fifteen.

source.what: Ordinance 75-58 (Civil Code), art. 310, Official Journal 1975 no. 78, French edition p. 832; Arabic edition of the same issue (https://www.joradp.dz/FTP/JO-ARABE/1975/A1975078.pdf) as quoted in the record (b4). The Arabic text is the official one; the gap is narrow (dentists are arguably doctors, architects arguably engineers).

attacks.quoteArabic: تتقادم بسنتين حقوق الاطباء، والصيادلة، والمحامين، والمهندسين والخبراء ، ووكلاء التفليسة ، والسماسرة، والاساتذة، والمعلمين
attacks.consequence: The question should not read as a closed list that a dentist's, architect's or midwife's lawyer would answer 'no' to; at least the record should note the French list and that d1 then gives a period seven times too long.

attacks.claim: d1 (15 years) excludes only wage claims. It still fires together with d6, d7 and d8 when claim_is_professional_fees, claim_is_trader_supply_or_hotel or claim_is_periodic_renewable_right is yes. The text of b1 gives way to a special text, and the 2-, 1- and 5-year periods are special texts. The result is a 15-year warning band on a claim whose real period is 1 to 5 years. d1 also stays silent for debts owed to the State (4 years, b45), where public_body_party is yes.
attacks.evidenceWords: فيما عدا الحالات التى ورد فيها نص خاص فى القانون وفيما عدا الاستثناءات الآتية

attacks.claim: d3 (1 year) and d4 (5 years) both fire on every wage claim with the same start date and the same warn effect. The two texts conflict. Only d3 is marked interpretive with readings, and d4 carries no flag and no readings. A wage claim 2 to 4 years old therefore gets a firm warning from d3 and nothing from d4, instead of one flagged ambiguity.
attacks.evidenceWords: يتقادم بخمس سنوات كل حق دورى متجدد ولو أقر به المدين كأجرة المبانى، والديون المتأخرة، والمرتبات والاجور

attacks.claim: The not-cited 316 para 3 says a period longer than five years does not run against persons lacking capacity, even if they have a legal representative. d1 and d2 (15 years) ignore it. No slot records the plaintiff's incapacity, absence or criminal sentence. A 15-year warning can fire when the period has not in fact run.
attacks.evidenceWords: ولا يسرى التقادم الذى تزيد مدته على خمس سنوات فى حق الاشخاص المذكورين فى الفقرة السابقة ولو كان لهم نائب قانونىّ طيلة مدة عدم أهليتهم

attacks.claim: The not-cited 316 para 2 says a period of less than five years does not run against persons without capacity, absent persons or persons serving criminal sentences who have no legal representative. It applies to the 1-year wage period of d3, and equally to d6 and d7. d3 has no condition for it. The not-cited 316 para 1 (a lawful impediment, or principal and representative) is also ignored.
attacks.evidenceWords: ولا يسرى التقادم الذى تنقضى مدته عن خمس سنوات فى حق عديمى الاهلية والغائبين والمحكوم عليهم بعقوبات جنائية اذا لم يكن لهم نائب قانونى

attacks.claim: d3 lists b21 among its bases, but the not-cited 319 para 2 is not applied. When a one-year debt was interrupted by the debtor's acknowledgment, the new period is fifteen years, not one. d3 has no slot or branch for an acknowledgment, so it can warn about a period that has become 15 years.
attacks.evidenceWords: أو اذا كان الدين يتقادم بسنة وانقطع تقادمه باقرار المدين، كانت مدة التقادم الجديد خمسة عشرة سنة

attacks.claim: The not-cited 309 para 2 sets a 15-year period for revenue owed by a bad-faith possessor or by the manager of jointly owned property. d8 treats every periodic renewable right as 5 years. A claim for revenue (ريع) owed by a bad-faith possessor, with claim_is_periodic_renewable_right yes, gets a 5-year warning that the text contradicts.
attacks.evidenceWords: غير أنه لا يسقط الريع المستحق في ذمة الحائز سىء النية، ولا الريع الواجب آداؤه على متصرف المال المشاع للمستحقين الا بانقضاء خمس عشرة سنة

attacks.claim: b10 says that if a written instrument is drawn up for a right of this kind, the period is fifteen years. d7 fires a 1-year warning (and d4, d6 and d8 their own periods) with no slot or exclusion for such an instrument. A claim backed by a written instrument gets a wrong short-period warning.
attacks.evidenceWords: واذا حرر سند بحق من هذه الحقوق فلا يتقادم الحق الا بانقضاء خمسة عشرة سنة

attacks.claim: d6 starts the period at the date the fee or expense fell due (b12). The adjacent cited rule b9 (313 para 1) starts the period when the creditors complete their services, even if they go on with others. b9 is not among d6's bases, so a continuing professional engagement gets the wrong start date. The literal text of 313 para 1 names articles 309 and 311, not 310 or 312. That mismatch should be flagged, not silently resolved.
attacks.evidenceWords: يبدأ سريان التقادم فى الحقوق المذكورة فى المادتين 309 و 311 من الوقت الذى يتم فيه الدائنون تقديـم خدماتهم ولو استمروا فى أداء خدمات أخرى

attacks.claim: d5 blocks a clean export outright. Its own text has a force majeure exception and a procedure for lifting the forfeiture (b38, b39), and raisedBy is only 'unclear'. The slot forfeiture_lifted_by_order is not in the slot list. No slot records force majeure or court-disruption events, so a lawful late claim is blocked and the lawyer cannot record the exception. A warning would fit better. With nonconciliation_record yes and the delivery date missing, the period cannot be computed, yet d5 still decides.
attacks.evidenceWords: باستثناء حالة القوة القاهرة أو وقوع أحداث من شأنها التأثير في السير العادي لمرفق العدالة

attacks.claim: b41 adds a condition ('the defendant missed two meetings in a row') that is not in the quoted paragraph 30 para 2. The quoted text only says a copy is handed to the plaintiff during the meeting. The condition comes from an uncited neighbouring paragraph. Since the delivery date drives d5's start, this changes when the 6 months begin.
attacks.evidenceWords: تسلم نسخة من المحضر الى المدعي اثناء الاجتماع

attacks.claim: None of the period rules handles interruption or suspension. All of them count from the due date or the act date. A debtor's acknowledgment, a command to pay, a seizure, a bankruptcy request or a judicial claim (even before a court without jurisdiction) restarts the period. There are no slots for any of these, so a debt that looks time-barred may be live, and the reverse. An acknowledgment of a 5-year debt does not extend it, but one of a 1-year debt makes it 15 years.
attacks.evidenceWords: ينقطع التقادم بالمطالبة القضائية ولو رفعت الدعوى الى محكمة غير مختصة بالتنبيه أو بالحجز

attacks.claim: b45 (4 years for taxes and dues owed to the State, with special start days) has no deadline item. The slot public_body_party exists but no rule uses it. A claim by the State for taxes or dues gets d1's 15-year warning instead of 4 years. Its starting days (end of the year for annual dues, end of the pleadings for judicial paper dues) are not modelled.
attacks.evidenceWords: تتقادم بأربع سنوات الضرائب، والرسوم المستحقة للدولة

attacks.claim: b17 says the long period does not run against 'the same persons while they lack capacity'. The text refers to all the persons named in the previous paragraph: persons without capacity, absent persons and persons serving criminal sentences. It also says the rule holds for the whole period of incapacity (طيلة مدة عدم أهليتهم). b17 narrows it to incapacity alone and drops absent persons and convicts.
attacks.evidenceWords: فى حق الاشخاص المذكورين فى الفقرة السابقة ولو كان لهم نائب قانونىّ طيلة مدة عدم أهليتهم

attacks.claim: Several slots exist that no period rule uses: employer_in_bankruptcy_or_settlement, worker_is_public_servant, work_accident_or_occupational_illness and defendant_resides_abroad. A wage or social claim by a public servant, or one tied to a work accident, may fall under a different regime. The rules neither route these cases nor warn that they are not covered.

The time limit is 6 months, running from the date of nonconciliation record delivered on; it is a forfeiture period, counted by the method excludeFirstAndLastDay; it applies when nonconciliation record is yes and (forfeiture lifted by order is unknown or forfeiture lifted by order is no). | partly: The TEXT does not state the applicability condition that an order lifting forfeiture is 'unknown' or 'no'. It expressly provides exceptions for force majeure and events affecting the normal administration of justice.

A limitation whose period falls short of five years does not run against persons without capacity, absent persons and persons serving criminal sentences who have no legal representative. | partly: The supplied wording does not state that the period is shorter than five years: it reads «تنقضى مدته عن خمس سنوات». The non-running rule, protected persons and absence of a legal representative are stated.

The time limit is 5 years, running from the date of debt due date; it is a limitation period, counted by the method excludeFirstDay; it applies when obligation is tort compensation is no and not (the petition asks for wages) and claim is periodic renewable right is yes. | partly: The TEXT does not state the applicability filters 'not tort compensation' and 'the petition does not ask for wages'.

The time limit is 1 year, running from the date of debt due date; it is a limitation period, counted by the method excludeFirstDay; it applies when obligation is tort compensation is no and not (the petition asks for wages) and claim is trader supply or hotel is yes. | partly: The TEXT does not state the 'not tort compensation' or 'no wage petition' filters. Its claim category is specifically supplies to persons who do not trade in them and the listed hotel/restaurant charges; reliance on the one-year limitation also requires the stated oath.

The time limit is 15 years, running from the date of debt due date; it is a limitation period, counted by the method excludeFirstDay; it applies when obligation is tort compensation is no and not (the petition asks for wages). | partly: The TEXT does not state that the two filters—no tort compensation and no wage petition—are sufficient for the fifteen-year rule. It expressly reserves «الحالات التى ورد فيها نص خاص فى القانون» and «الاستثناءات الآتية».

Where the defendant missed two meetings in a row, a copy of the non-conciliation record is handed to the plaintiff during the meeting. | partly: The TEXT says only that a copy of the record is handed to the plaintiff during the meeting. It does not state that the defendant missed two consecutive meetings or identify the record as a non-conciliation record.

The time limit is 2 years, running from the date of debt due date; it is a limitation period, counted by the method excludeFirstDay; it applies when obligation is tort compensation is no and not (the petition asks for wages) and claim is professional fees is yes. | partly: The TEXT does not state the 'not tort compensation' or 'no wage petition' filters. The two-year rule concerns the named professions' professional work and expenses, rather than professional fees generally.
